subject: MSA / Order Form redlines — defend allocation and approval path
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena.martin@brightforge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@brightforge.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightForge - MSA redlines (defend allocation)

Hi Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attaching BrightForge's redlines (brightforge_msa_redlines_v2.docx) and a short summary PDF. Key commercial/legal asks from our side:

- BrightForge to have right to control the defense for third-party IP infringement claims that arise from our use of the Platform (we propose right-to-defend with conduct/counsel oversight).
- Reasonable cooperation from Redwood (technical evidence, preservation of logs, engineer availability) and a 30‑day cure/notice window.
- Insurance offset: BrightForge expects Redwood's liability to be reduced by insurance recoveries; we propose limited carveouts for willful misconduct.
- Narrow the "AI output" carve-in language so BrightForge doesn't inherit downstream output liability for customer data they upload.

We'd like to get to a commercial compromise this week if possible — do you have proposed bridging language for the defense/control paragraph and an approval path for exec signoff?

Thanks,
Elena Martin
Outside Counsel, BrightForge Systems
(elena.martin@brightforge.com)

Attachment: brightforge_msa_redlines_v2.docx (MS Word redline)
Attachment: orderform_proposed_changes_summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Martin <elena.martin@brightforge.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@brightforge.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightForge - MSA redlines (defend allocation)

Ben / Laura —

Forwarding BrightForge's redlines. High-level take: their defend-control ask is standard commercial pushback but they push for broad control + insurance offset. We should:

1) Propose a limited right-to-defend for third-party IP claims tied to claims that solely concern BrightForge's data/use and requiring Redwood's consent when Redwood's indemnity exposure exceeds $250k.
2) Keep cooperation obligations but add a "reasonably available" engineer clause to limit on-call expectations.
3) Offer an insurance-offset formula that preserves Redwood's indemnity dollar-for-dollar but excludes proceeds attributable to Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Ben — need your read on whether the $250k consent threshold is acceptable commercially.
Laura — can you draft a redline with the bridging paragraph and the approval route: Legal -> Sales Lead -> GC signoff. If Sales lead (Ben) signs off, I'll route to GC for final approval.

I'll keep BrightForge on copy for transparency, but let's keep internal discussion in replies-to-all to preserve thread trace.

–Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Martin <elena.martin@brightforge.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T13:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightForge - MSA redlines (defend allocation)

Kim — thanks. Quick commercial notes:

- $250k consent threshold is OK as a starting point; if they push back, we can escalate to $500k.
- We need an explicit SLA cut: if defense costs are > $500k, Redwood reserves right to assume defense or require escrow/custody of damages.
- Timeline: BrightForge wants to sign this month — I can escalate to my director for fast-track approval once Legal gives us the redline.

Action: Laura, please prepare the proposed paragraph and call out the fallback if they refuse the threshold. I can join a 30-min call with Elena tomorrow afternoon to negotiate.

—Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena.martin@brightforge.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightForge - MSA redlines (defend allocation)

Elena / team —

Thanks for the redlines. Per Kimberly and Ben's feedback, attached below is a short compromise paragraph we recommend inserting into Section 9 (Indemnification / Third‑Party IP Claims). If BrightForge is comfortable with this approach, we can prepare a tracked-change doc for signatures and route via HubSpot/DocuSign for exec approval.

Proposed bridging language (draft):
"Redwood will indemnify, defend and hold harmless Customer from and against any Losses finally awarded to a third‑party in a claim alleging that Customer's use of the Service in accordance with this Agreement infringes a third‑party's intellectual property rights; provided that Customer provides prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation. If the indemnifiable claim would, based on reasonable good faith estimates, expose Redwood to aggregate liability in excess of Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (US $250,000), Redwood shall have the right to assume control of the defense. Any insurance recoveries applicable to the claim shall first be used to reduce the indemnified Losses, except where such recoveries are attributable to Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Notes: this preserves a Customer-friendly right-to-defend for smaller claims while protecting Redwood on large exposures. We added the "reasonable good faith estimate" language to avoid gaming. Also added the "first used to reduce" insurance-offset language but carved out Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct.

Attachments: proposed_bridge_paragraph.txt (plain text), next_steps_checklist.pdf (internal routing steps)

Next steps:
- Elena: please confirm by EOD if BrightForge can live with $250k threshold.
- Ben: if they accept, I'll prepare a tracked change MSA and route to you and Kimberly for internal approval (Legal -> Sales Lead -> GC).

Laura Bennett
Legal Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
